references.source: fixed in configuration: the test market's genesis rate, tINR/tUSD · 0.30% · deep at 84.00 tINR per tUSD, ± 0.5%; no trade moves it

authorityBudget.statement: 18.97 tINR available = granted 30.00 (base 10.00, owner grants 20.00) + earned 0.00 − used 11.03 (payments 8.07, conversion costs 2.96, promises paid 0.00) − promised and not yet paid 0.00 − reserved for certificates not yet used 0.00
limits: Earned means paid for, through the escrow, by a client this workspace does not know to be its own: a client the wallet has never seen cannot be told apart from an unregistered address of a member (D7 assumption A-ID; a second workspace counts as the workspace's own only when it shares a member's passkey).
Conversions count only their cost against a fixed reference band, so the mandate's own limits on amounts per payment, per period and over its life are what bound how much can be converted.

receiptChain.note: Every receipt up to this case's last one: its number, its predecessor's hash and its own. Bodies are carried only for this case's receipts, so a verifier recomputes those and checks the links of the rest.

verification.note: A vault job is recorded by the vault service, not in the wallet's receipt chain: its decision records are hash-chained there, and each one this case carries is re-hashed by the verifier. The wallet's receipt chain and ledger as a whole were verified too when the case was assembled.

redactions.why: Password hashes, recovery codes, session tokens and the vault service's bearer token are not part of any case.
The hash of the session an approval was given in, sign-in times and user agents are not needed to judge a decision.
Recovery codes, contacts and requests have nothing to do with a money decision.

redactions.how: replaced by "sha256:" and the first 16 hex digits of their SHA-256
redactions.why: That is enough to tell passkeys apart; the public key, which a verifier needs, is kept.
The audit log's IP addresses are not needed to judge a decision.

redactions.how: never held by this API; addresses only
redactions.why: The agent, co-signer, guardian and relayer keys stay in the vault service.

cannotProve: No model took part in this job: the owner asked for it directly, or the engine ran it under authority the owner wrote.

The transactions are on a local Anvil chain (chain id 31337) started for this installation, with valueless test tokens. Their hashes are not publicly verifiable; they can be re-read only from that chain while it runs (verify-evidence.ts --rpc).
The passkey's make is not attested (its AAGUID is all zeros): a signature proves possession of the key, not which device or software held it.

A forger who rewrites this file and recomputes every hash makes a file that is consistent in itself. Compare its root with one obtained independently (verify-evidence.ts --root), check the receipt-chain head against a fresh read (--head), or re-read the transactions from the chain (--rpc).
No one outside this work has reviewed the code that made these records (server/readiness.ts lists this as a standing blocker).

hashes.algorithm: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of each part (keys sorted, no spaces: shared/sha256.ts canonical); the root covers the envelope and every part's hash
